label: D2 after choosing a1 and landing in S2 (a1 rare transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the last-action input is a1 and the shown state is S2, i.e. the rare transition after choosing a1. All inputs are observed at D2, so no future variables are used. Dev: P=0.87, R=0.999, F1=0.93, mass recall 1.0. It never fires at D1 or GO, on a1->S1 (common), or on any a2 trial (27 tiny misses, about 0 mass). About 13% of a1->S2 steps stay silent; this is weakly tied to the hidden good state being S2 and to late-episode trials (80+). Adding good==1 lowers F1 to 0.85. Magnitude is fairly uniform (median 0.77 of max). Coverage across activation quartiles is flat whether or not prev_reward==1 and whether or not the previous choice was a1, so neither of those modulates magnitude. No a2->S1 counterpart fires on this feature.

issues: Most of the firing claims hold. On dev, D1 and GO have 0 active steps; in_rew=1 has 0; a1->S1 has 0; a2->S1 has 0 mass. The original predicate's test score is P 0.865, R 0.999, F1 0.927, mass recall 1.0, matching what was reported.

The false positives are not 'weakly tied' to late trials; they are a sharp episode-time cutoff. Precision of the predicate by ep_trial on dev: 1.0 for ep_trial<60, 1.0 for 60-70, 0.999 for 70-80, 0.573 for 80-90, 0.002 for 90-100. Almost all of the roughly 13% silent a1->S2 steps fall at ep_trial of about 85 or later.

'Magnitude is fairly uniform' is false: magnitude falls steadily over the episode. Coverage by activation quartile (low to high) on dev: ep_bucket<4 (trials 0-9) [0, 0, 0.006, 0.286], ep_trial<30 [0, 0.002, 0.256, 0.977], ep_trial 30-60 [0.014, 0.713, 0.744, 0.023], ep_trial>=60 [0.983, 0.285, 0, 0]. Early-episode a1->S2 steps hold the top quartile and late ones the bottom quartile, until the feature goes silent near trial 86.
The good-state link is a side effect. Adding good==1 gives flat quartile coverage (0.85 / 0.84 / 0.82 / 0.82) and lowers F1 to 0.851, so the good state does not explain the misses; episode time does.
The claims that prev_reward and prev_action do not modulate magnitude are roughly right: quartile coverage is flat for both.

After adding the cutoff, test misses and false positives (410 / 552 steps, 0.1% of the activation mass) are scattered boundary noise around trial 86. Most missed activations are tiny (about 0.05 to 0.2 of max) on context-trial a1->S2 steps.
